correctness.rationale: For every prime q|b-1, the p-1 forbidden residues for c modulo q do not exhaust q, because either q|d leaves one forbidden class or q≥p. CRT yields 0≤c≤b-2 with gcd(b-1,1+c+jd)=1. The short-width bound gives x_j=c+jd<2b, hence s_b(x_j)=x_j-(b-1)e_j for e_j∈{0,1}; simultaneous m≡1 mod q-1 makes b^m≡b modulo all digit-sum prime factors. A hypothetical common factor divides (b-1)(1+e_j), supported only on primes of b-1 since b odd, contradicting CRT. The known p-divisibility obstruction gives sharpness; independent full-integer checks for b=11 and 21 d=4 plus modular witnesses at further bases corroborate.
residual_risks: Only sufficient short-stride domain (p-2)d≤b+1; does not solve all even strides.
